changelog.summary: Handing a session between apps of one project: connectWithAccessToken(token) / useSocialAuth().signInWithAccessToken(token) adopts a Decane access token another app handed over (in a URL), signed in at once and unlocked on the first signature — with deferDeviceProtection that prompts for nothing; the session lasts as long as the token and ends with session-expired. Everything the client persists (identity, last signed-out user, live session) is now keyed by the app id rather than the API key, so two apps of one project under different keys on one origin see the same signed-in user and a same-tab navigation between them resumes the full session; entries written under the old key are read once and moved. New InvalidAccessTokenError (INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN).

Deferred wallet protection: deferDeviceProtection (DecaneConnectConfig and SocialConfig) makes sign-in ask for no passkey or password — the wallet is created and the session opens with no stored device share — and the new protectDevice() wraps and stores one later, at the app's own moment (before the first transaction, say): passkey where the device can hold one, otherwise promptUnlockPassword. Resolves false on a dismissed prompt rather than throwing. deviceProtected() reports whether this device holds a wrapped share. Both on useSocialWallet(). Until protected, a device has no passkey/password unlock and every visit is a full sign-in; recovery is unchanged. The server's wallet_created event records unlockMethod "deferred".

Signing back in after sign-out: disconnect() now remembers WHICH account signed out (a userId, a lookup key and not a credential), so canSignInWithPasskey()/canUnlockWithPassword() and their sign-in twins offer that account's own passkey or password back even when several accounts are enrolled on one browser — previously, with more than one enrolled, the kit refused to guess and both read false. New forgetLastUser() is "use a different account": drops the memory, leaves device shares untouched; on useSocialWallet() it also recomputes canUsePasskey. connect()/unlock() keep the strict lookup. The llms.txt hook references were also brought up to the real return shapes (31 members were missing, across passkey, password, recovery, typed-data, balances and access token).

Phone-number sign-in via SMS (Termii). connectWithPhone(phone) + verifyPhoneCode(phone, code), 'phone' in authMethods, and a phone form in both built-in UIs. Numbers must be E.164 (+2348012345678) — local formats are rejected rather than guessed at, because the wallet is derived from the number and inferring a country would merge two users onto one wallet or split one across two. Identity is HMAC(E.164), so a phone user is a DIFFERENT user from the same human's email or Google sign-in, exactly as email and Google already differ. Available in all three SDKs.

Sign-in now returns the provider's profile: ConnectResult gains an optional `profile` of { name?, email?, picture? }, so apps can greet the user by name instead of by address. It is passed through from the verified Google or KingsChat response and never stored — the backend keeps only an HMAC and a masked identifier — so it is available at sign-in and nowhere else. Absent entirely for email sign-in. Expo SDK 0.2.0 has the same field. useSocialAuth() exposes it as `profile`, null until a sign-in returns one and not restored across reloads.

KingsChat sign-in now requests only the profile scope by default, in both the web and Expo SDKs. It previously asked for send_chat_message, which put 'post as you' on a consent screen whose only job is to log the user in. Pass `scopes` explicitly if your app actually sends chat messages.

React Native / Expo SDK released as decane-connect-kit-expo (see llms-expo.txt). Server-assisted recovery is now always on — a user who reinstalls gets their wallet back from signing in alone, so the serverAssistedRecovery option was removed. Google sign-in on mobile uses an in-app auth sheet needing nothing registered in Google Cloud. Adds connectWithGoogleToken() so native Google Sign-In resolves to the SAME wallet as the web redirect flow, and connectWithKingsChat().

Optional per-signature authority: requireAssertionPerSignature makes every signature need a fresh passkey assertion, verified inside the TEE against a single-use 60s challenge, instead of an unlocked session signing freely until expiry. The session still stays warm — this does NOT shorten sessionDurationMinutes. Available on both DecaneConnectConfig and SocialConfig. Default false, so existing behaviour is unchanged. Requires TEE signer v0.2.3+.

Custom auth: sign in with a JWT from your own issuer (Auth0, Clerk, Firebase, Cognito, or your own backend). Adds DecaneConnect.connectWithToken(token, opts?), SocialConfig.customAuth, and useSocialAuth().signInWithToken / .signInWithCustomAuth. Backward compatible — no existing API changed.
Baseline for this manifest. Wallet connect (EVM, Solana, Tron, Bitcoin) plus non-custodial social sign-in via Google and email, TEE-backed signing, 2-of-3 Shamir recovery.

Base URL resolution treats an empty value as unset at every step (apiBase option, DECANE_API_BASE env, then the built-in https://backend.decane.app). Deploy templates that write `DECANE_API_BASE: ${DECANE_API_BASE:-}` land an empty string, which 1.3.0 took as the base and sent every request to a relative URL ("Failed to parse URL from /share/addresses"). The resolved base is now readable as client.apiBase.
Server-side phone sign-in: connectWithPhone(phone) + verifyPhoneCode(phone, code), mirroring the email OTP pair. New SMS_NOT_CONFIGURED error code for deployments with no SMS provider.

Server-side sign-in: connectWithEmail/verifyEmailCode (email OTP), connectWithGoogleToken, connectWithKingsChatToken, connectWithToken (custom auth), getKingsChatConfig, revokeAccessToken. New `apiKey` option (env DECANE_API_KEY) and DecaneApiError with backend error codes. DecaneAddresses gains `tron`; DecaneLinkedAccount.chainType widens to include "tron" — exhaustive switches need a tron arm. Verify-only usage is unchanged and still needs no apiKey.
Baseline: verifyAccessToken (static ES256 key or JWKS), safeVerifyAccessToken, getAddresses, getUser, standalone verifyAccessToken.

connect.$comment: Server-to-server provisioning API for agencies/builders: one project + API key per end-client. Path-versioned, not package-versioned.

changelog.summary: Several sign-in callbacks per key: callback_urls[] on POST /clients, POST /clients/:ref/keys and PATCH /clients/:ref/keys/:keyId (replaced whole, like allowed_origins), and on key rows. /auth/google/init and /auth/x/init pick the entry whose host matches the request's Origin (or Referer) — exact host with port first, then hostname — and fall back to the first entry, so one key serves an app from its domain, a preview host and localhost. The single callback_url is still accepted everywhere and reported as the first entry.

Initial release. Organization tier above projects, with org-scoped provisioning tokens (dck_org_) minted from the dashboard's Organization page. POST /connect/v1/clients creates a client's project and first API key in one transaction, idempotent on your own external_ref. Keys minted here are origin_policy=strict: a non-empty allowed_origins list is required and a request carrying neither Origin nor Referer is refused, closing the replay of a key scraped from a published bundle. Deprovision archives AND revokes every key; there is no hard-delete, because destroying a project cascades to end users' wallet shares.
